title: Add batches to the audit trail without breaking its users

blocks.text: Version 2 of the company's audit library adds `appendAll(batch)` to the `AuditTrail` interface. Twelve teams implement `AuditTrail` in their own code, written against version 1: an in-memory trail for tests, one that writes to a file, one that forwards to a message queue. None of them will change their classes for this release.

The payments service records each transfer as a batch, the debit and then the credit, on its `LockedTrail`. A compliance report reads `entries()` on its own thread, and an auditor once flagged a debit with no credit in a report.

items: `AuditTrail.appendAll`, which every team's trail gets without changing a line;

blocks.text: Keep `append` and `entries` as they are. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a batch recorded on the locked trail follows the earlier entries, in order
a trail written before batches existed takes a batch unchanged, through its own append
a report reading the locked trail while a batch is being recorded sees all of the batch or none of it

origin.section: A Default Method Keeps Implementations Compiling, and Runs Code That Never Saw Their Locks

concepts: An inherited default runs without the implementation's own rules, such as its lock, so a class with such rules overrides it.
A default method lets implementations written before it compile and work unchanged.
